source_row.rationale: For adults, prolonged grief disorder is considered when a close person's death occurred at least 12 months earlier and persistent longing or preoccupation is associated with significant distress or functional impairment. Option B is the condition to evaluate; the full DSM-5-TR criteria and cultural context must still be assessed. The other choices do not fit this persistent bereavement pattern.
source_row.source_detail: Symptoms and Diagnosis: persistent intense longing and/or preoccupation with the deceased with significant distress or functional impairment; for adults the death must have occurred at least one year earlier, and diagnosis requires the full DSM-5-TR criteria with cultural context considered. APA page physician-reviewed August 2025; DSM-5-TR (2022) remains current and includes prolonged grief disorder; live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Psychosocial Integrity: mental-health symptom recognition, therapeutic communication, professional boundaries, coping and psychosocial support as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: An adult's spouse died 14 months ago. The client has persistent intense longing, preoccupation with the death, and major impairment in daily functioning. Which condition should be evaluated?
